examples.ko: 우리 집은 당뇨 가족력이 있어서 검사를 자주 받아요.
examples.en: Diabetes runs in my family, so I get tested often.
There was a box at the hospital to write down family medical history.
Even without a family history, you still need to take care of your health.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 암 가족력이 있는지 물어보셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor asked whether there is a family history of cancer.

examples.ko: 가족력이 있으면 일찍 검진을 받는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: If it runs in your family, it is good to get checked early.

examples.ko: 할아버지 때부터 고혈압 가족력이 이어져 왔어요.
examples.en: High blood pressure has run in our family since my grandfather's time.

explain: 병원 문진표에 자주 나오는 말로, 가족 중에 같은 병을 앓은 사람이 있는지를 말해요. '가족력이 있다/없다'로 쓰고, 병 이름을 앞에 붙여 '당뇨 가족력'처럼 말해요. 가족이 같은 병을 앓았다는 사실을 말할 뿐이어서 '유전'이라는 말과는 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: There is no family history of heart disease for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족 중에 같은 병을 앓은 사람이 없을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when no family member has had the same illness.

phrases.example: 암 가족력이 있으면 검진을 일찍 받는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: If you have a family history of cancer, it's better to get checkups early.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병 이름을 앞에 붙여 어떤 병의 가족력인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the disease name first to say which illness runs in the family.

phrases.en: The doctor asked about my family medical history.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 진료받을 때 자주 듣는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase you often hear at the hospital.

explain_en: It often appears on medical questionnaires and refers to whether family members have had the same illness. You say '가족력이 있다/없다' and put the illness first, as in '당뇨 가족력'. It only states that relatives had the illness, so it feels different from '유전' (heredity).

examples.ko: 할아버지는 오래된 만성병 때문에 약을 드세요.
examples.en: Grandfather takes medicine for a long-standing chronic disease.
For chronic diseases, steady management is the most important thing.

examples.ko: 당뇨나 고혈압 같은 만성병이 있으면 정기 검진을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: If you have a chronic disease like diabetes or high blood pressure, you need regular checkups.

examples.ko: 만성병을 가진 사람이 늘고 있다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that the number of people with chronic diseases is rising.
My father has a chronic condition, so he is careful about his diet.

examples.ko: 만성병에는 생활 습관을 바꾸는 게 큰 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: For chronic diseases, changing your lifestyle helps a lot.

explain: 오래 낫지 않고 계속 관리해야 하는 병을 말해요. 뉴스나 병원에서는 '만성 질환'이라고도 하고, 반대로 갑자기 생겨 빨리 진행되는 병은 '급성'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 만성 질환이 있으면 정기 검진이 필요해요.
phrases.en: If you have a chronic illness, you need regular checkups.
phrases.nuance_ko: '만성병'과 같은 뜻으로, 병원이나 뉴스에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 만성병, used more in hospitals and news.

phrases.en: My father has a chronic disease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 관리해야 하는 병이 있다는 사실을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone has a long-term condition.

phrases.en: I manage my chronic disease with exercise and diet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료보다 꾸준히 돌보는 것을 강조할 때 '관리하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '관리하다' emphasizes ongoing care rather than a cure.

explain_en: It refers to an illness that doesn't go away and must be managed continuously. In the news or at hospitals it is also called '만성 질환', and an illness that comes suddenly and progresses quickly is called '급성'.

examples.en: I got stung by a bee and my arm swelled up.
I got stung by a bee in the mountains and it really hurts.

examples.ko: 손등에 벌침이 박혀 있어서 빼 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: A stinger was stuck in the back of my hand, so I asked someone to pull it out.

examples.ko: 저는 벌침 알레르기가 있어서 늘 조심해요.
examples.en: I'm allergic to bee stings, so I'm always careful.

examples.ko: 벌침을 빼려면 카드로 살살 긁어 보세요.
examples.en: To remove the stinger, gently scrape it with a card.
My younger sibling went to the hospital because of a bee sting.

explain: 다쳤다고 말할 때는 '벌에 쏘이다'가 더 일상적이에요. '벌침'은 쏘는 침 자체나 그 상처를 말할 때 자연스러워요. '벌침에 쏘이다', '벌침을 빼다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.en: I got stung by a bee in the park and went to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벌에 쏘이다'가 더 일상적이지만, 침을 강조할 때 '벌침에 쏘이다'도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '벌에 쏘이다' is more everyday, but 벌침에 쏘이다 is also used when stressing the stinger.
phrases.en_equiv: to be stung by a bee

phrases.en: I carefully pulled out the stinger stuck in my skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 남은 침을 뽑는 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for pulling out the stinger left in the body.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is allergic to bee stings, so he is careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 건강 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in medical and health talk.

explain_en: When you say you got hurt, '벌에 쏘이다' is the more everyday phrase. '벌침' sounds natural when you mean the stinger itself or the sting wound. It pairs with verbs like '벌침에 쏘이다' and '벌침을 빼다'.

examples.ko: 이 텀블러는 보온이 잘 돼서 겨울에 따뜻한 차를 넣어 다녀요.
examples.en: This tumbler keeps heat well, so I carry warm tea in it in winter.

examples.ko: 담요로 감싸면 음식을 오래 보온할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you wrap it in a blanket, you can keep the food warm for a long time.

examples.ko: 아기 방을 보온하려고 두꺼운 커튼을 달았어요.
examples.en: I hung thick curtains to keep the baby's room warm.

examples.ko: 이 외투는 보온해 주는 효과가 커요.
examples.en: This coat is very good at keeping you warm.
I kept the whole pot warm so the soup wouldn't get cold.
They say an air layer is important for keeping things warm.

explain: 차갑게 식은 것을 데우는 것이 아니라, 이미 있는 따뜻함이 빠져나가지 않게 지키는 것이에요. '보온병', '보온 도시락'처럼 명사로도 많이 쓰고, 반대로 시원함을 지키는 것은 '보냉'이라고 해요. '데우다'와 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: I brought warm water in a thermos.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨거운 음료를 오래 따뜻하게 두는 병이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bottle that keeps hot drinks warm for a long time.

phrases.example: 이 이불은 보온이 잘 돼서 겨울에 좋아요.
phrases.en: This blanket keeps heat well, so it's good for winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따뜻함이 잘 유지된다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise how well something keeps warmth in.

phrases.en: I stuck plastic on the window to keep the room warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따뜻함을 지키려는 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the purpose of keeping heat in.

explain_en: It is not about heating something cold but about keeping existing warmth from escaping. As a noun it appears in '보온병' and '보온 도시락', and keeping something cool is '보냉'. Don't confuse it with '데우다' (to heat up).

examples.ko: 어머니가 꽃 모양 브로치를 선물해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother gave me a flower-shaped brooch as a gift.
The mood changed after I pinned a brooch on my coat.
I inherited this brooch from my grandmother.
I don't know where my brooch fell off.

examples.ko: 옷깃에 작은 브로치 하나만 달아도 예뻐요.
examples.en: Even just one small brooch on the collar looks pretty.
The brooch pin is weak, so it keeps coming off.

explain: '브로치를 달다', '브로치를 꽂다'처럼 말해요. 목에 거는 목걸이나 손가락에 끼는 반지와는 함께 쓰는 동사가 달라요.

phrases.en: I pinned a brooch on my collar.
phrases.nuance_ko: '달다'와 같은 뜻이고, 핀으로 찌르듯 고정하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as 달다, with the feel of fixing it on with a pin.

phrases.en: I gave my friend a brooch for her birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 브로치를 선물로 줄 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the phrase for giving a brooch as a gift.
phrases.en_equiv: to give a brooch as a gift

phrases.en: That brooch is really pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 브로치를 칭찬할 때 조사 '가'와 함께 쓰는 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a sentence for praising a brooch, using the particle 가.

explain_en: You say '브로치를 달다' or '브로치를 꽂다'. The verbs differ from those used with a necklace (worn around the neck) or a ring (put on a finger).

examples.en: On Lunar New Year, the children wore colorful jeogori and bowed to their elders.
That striped-sleeve jeogori is really lovely.
The saekdong jeogori is usually worn by young children.
At the first-birthday party, I saw a baby dressed in a saekdong jeogori.
I picked a skirt that goes well with the saekdong jeogori.
It's a blanket as colorful as a saekdong jeogori.

explain: 소매에 여러 색 줄무늬를 댄 한복 저고리예요. 보통 명절이나 돌에 아이들이 입는 옷으로 떠올려요. '저고리'는 한복의 윗옷을 말해요.

phrases.en: The baby wore a saekdong jeogori at the first birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입을 때는 '입다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '입다' (to wear) for clothing.

phrases.example: 색동저고리에 분홍 치마를 입은 아이가 인사했어요.
phrases.en: A child in a saekdong jeogori and a pink skirt said hello.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저고리와 같이 입는 아래옷인 '치마'를 같이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mention the skirt, the bottom worn together with the jeogori.

phrases.en: The saekdong jeogori is so lovely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '곱다'는 색이나 모양이 부드럽고 예쁠 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: '곱다' fits when colors or shapes look soft and pretty.

explain_en: It is a hanbok jacket with multicolored stripes on the sleeves. People usually picture it as clothing children wear on holidays or first birthdays. '저고리' is the upper garment of a hanbok.

examples.en: I apply foundation thinly on my face.
This foundation sticks well to the skin.
The foundation shade is too dark for me.

examples.ko: 새 파운데이션을 사려고 화장품 가게에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the cosmetics shop to buy a new foundation.
I ran out of foundation.
I asked my friend to recommend a foundation.

explain: 피부색을 고르게 하는 화장품이고, 가게에서는 '쿠션'이나 '비비크림'과 같이 비교해서 골라요. 색은 '21호', '23호'처럼 호수로 말해요.

phrases.en: I use foundation shade 21.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색은 호수로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shades are named by number.

phrases.en: I picked a foundation that suits my skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 살 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often used when shopping.

phrases.en: It's summer, so I changed my foundation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절이나 피부에 따라 다른 제품으로 쓸 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when switching products by season or skin condition.

explain_en: It is a makeup product for evening out skin tone, and in shops people compare it with 쿠션 and 비비크림. Shades are given by number, like '21호' and '23호'.
